clips.text_zh: SpaceX IPO 第三輪 lockup 9 月 9 日到期，約 2.4% 股數解禁。319M 股一齊湧出嚟，供應一定唔細。又係學費。
clips.text_en_b1: On September 9, 2026, about 319 million SpaceX shares — roughly 7% of the baseline IPO pool, or about 2.4% of total shares outstanding — become eligible for sale. This is the 90th trading day after the IPO and marks the third major lockup release event. Holders will be able to dump on the market.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread tracking the third SpaceX lockup expiry on Sep 9 2026

signal.rationale: Calendar event noted, no trade setup given — wait to see supply impact

clips.text_en_b2: On September 9, 2026, roughly 319 million SpaceX shares — accounting for around 7% of the baseline IPO pool and approximately 2.4% of total shares outstanding — will become eligible for sale. Because this marks the third major lockup release on the 90th trading day after the IPO, holders are bracing for a significant supply dump. With that much stock flooding the market, the selling pressure could easily catch retail investors off guard.
clips.text_en_c1: On September 9, 2026, roughly 319 million SpaceX shares — amounting to approximately 7% of the baseline IPO allocation or 2.4% of total shares outstanding — will become eligible for resale. The date falls on the ninetieth session following the listing and represents the third significant lockup expiration since the offering was priced. Once the restriction lapses, insiders and pre-IPO backers will be free to liquidate their positions into an already fragile secondary market, an arrangement that, in all likelihood, will exert considerable downward pressure on the share price. Investors who entered during the early stages ought to brace themselves for the inevitable supply glut.
clips.text_en_c2: On the ninetieth trading day following SpaceX's IPO — September 9, 2026 — the third major lockup tranche expires, releasing roughly 319 million shares into circulation. That figure constitutes approximately seven percent of the baseline IPO pool and a non-trivial 2.4 percent of total shares outstanding, a quantity sufficient to overwhelm bid-side liquidity if holders elect to liquidate in concert. Insiders who purchased at the offering price now enjoy an unrestricted exit, and the market must absorb what amounts to a forced seller of considerable magnitude. Whether the float is digested gradually or dumped en masse will, in all likelihood, dictate the near-term trajectory of the stock. For late entrants, the lesson, as ever, is invariably expensive.

clips.text_zh: 10年 holding 一個，BTC 定 gold？我揀 BTC，但每次問完自己都會心虛。CFD 開 gold 輸緊，唔該唔好再問。
clips.text_en_b1: If you had to hold only one asset for the next ten years, would you pick Bitcoin or gold? What makes your choice better than the other? Think about supply, adoption, and how each has behaved through past cycles. Which one survives the next decade intact?
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread asking which asset to hold for 10 years, BTC or gold

signal.rationale: Implicit long bias on BTC over gold, decade-scale thesis

clips.text_en_b2: If you were forced to hold only one asset for the next decade, would you go with Bitcoin or gold? What concrete factors actually justify your pick over the other? Consider how each has weathered past cycles, where institutional adoption currently stands, and what long-term scarcity looks like under various economic scenarios. Which one genuinely survives the next ten years intact, and which one gets left behind?
clips.text_en_c1: If one were compelled to select a single asset and hold it for the next decade, the choice between Bitcoin and gold would test one's conviction more than one's portfolio theory. Bitcoin's fixed issuance schedule and accelerating institutional integration suggest asymmetric upside, yet its volatility and dependence on continuous liquidity remain genuine concerns. Gold, by contrast, has weathered millennia of monetary experimentation, though its real returns have historically lagged risk assets over comparable horizons. Were survivability through geopolitical fragmentation the principal criterion, the calculus might tilt the other way, and an existing CFD position bleeding money hardly clarifies matters.
clips.text_en_c2: Were one compelled to hold a single asset across the coming decade, the choice between Bitcoin and gold would expose the fault lines of one's entire investment philosophy. Gold offers millennia of monetary trust, a finite physical supply, and the dull ballast of central-bank demand; Bitcoin promises programmatic scarcity, a twenty-four-hour global market, and an adoption curve that, however volatile, has historically rewarded patience through prior cycles. The purist argues that gold's industrial utility is negligible and its custodianship antiquated; the contrarian counters that no digital ledger has yet endured a genuine sovereign confiscation event. Both critiques carry weight, and the honest holder admits, perhaps grudgingly, that conviction in either camp requires a leap of faith no spreadsheet can quite justify.

clips.topic_zh: MIT 警告 AI 滅民主
clips.text_zh: MIT 經濟學家出 paper 講 AI 自動化會令財富集中、工人反抗，最後統治精英用 repression。睇到標題已經覺得係佢自己份糧。AI 真係遲早殺埋我呢行。
clips.text_en_b1: A Nobel-winning MIT economist published a paper called 'Automation and Repression'. It argues that as AI replaces human labor, wealth concentrates heavily in the hands of a tiny group of capital owners. Inequality skyrockets, the threat of revolt spikes, and the ruling elite turns to repression to protect itself.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread on a MIT paper warning that AI automation leads to inequality and repression

signal.rationale: Macro opinion piece, not a trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: A Nobel-winning MIT economist has published a paper titled 'Automation and Repression' arguing that, as AI steadily replaces human labor, wealth will concentrate dramatically in the hands of a small elite. Although inequality skyrockets and the threat of mass revolt spikes accordingly, the paper suggests that ruling elites will ultimately resort to repression rather than redistributing power.
clips.text_en_c1: A Nobel laureate affiliated with MIT has published a working paper entitled 'Automation and Repression', in which he contends that accelerating AI deployment will progressively displace human labor across an entire economy, precipitating an unprecedented concentration of capital among a narrow stratum of asset holders. As inequality widens and the latent threat of popular insurrection intensifies, the governing elite, the paper argues, will ultimately resort to coercive instruments to safeguard their accumulated privileges. Cynics have already dismissed the thesis as a thinly veiled justification of the author's own professional relevance, though the trajectory it outlines is uncomfortably plausible for those whose livelihoods depend on automatable cognitive labor.
clips.text_en_c2: A Nobel laureate from MIT's economics faculty has circulated a working paper provocatively titled 'Automation and Repression,' in which he contends that accelerating artificial intelligence will precipitate an unprecedented concentration of capital among a vanishingly small owner class. As wage labour is progressively rendered obsolete, inequality metastasises, the latent threat of popular revolt intensifies, and the governing elite — confronted with diminishing legitimacy — resorts to coercive instruments of state power to safeguard its position. Cynics have noted, with some justification, that the author's professional incentives are scarcely orthogonal to the conclusions he advances. Whether or not the thesis survives peer review, its central proposition is unsettling: the same technological substrate that promises liberation may, under sufficient economic stress, furnish the machinery for its abolition.

clips.text_zh: Elon 話 chess 太多步數，叫 AI 代打，俾 Chess.com 官 account 連環 ratio 佢。最後仲話人哋係 intern。連 Elon 都開始 online 崩潰，呢個世界真係睇唔晒。
clips.text_en_b1: Elon Musk complained that chess has too many possible moves for humans. Chess.com's official account ratio'd him three times in a row. He then tried to cope by saying robot chess will be better, and belittled the person running the account by calling them an intern. The community found the meltdown genuinely pathetic.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread on Elon getting ratio'd by Chess.com over a chess take

signal.rationale: Celebrity online drama, no market setup

clips.text_en_b2: Elon Musk publicly complained that chess contains far too many possible moves for any human to track properly. Chess.com's official account ratio'd him three times in rapid succession, after which he tried to save face by insisting robotic chess will eventually surpass the human game. He then belittled the person running the account by dismissing them as an intern, while the community watched the meltdown unfold in real time.
clips.text_en_c1: Elon Musk recently took to social media to lament that chess, owing to its astronomical branching factor, is fundamentally unsuited to human cognition and ought to be left to artificial engines. Chess.com's official account proceeded to ratio him on three consecutive occasions, a sequence that prompted him to pivot toward claiming that robot-versus-robot chess will inevitably eclipse human play, before dismissing the operator behind the account as a mere intern. Observers across the broader community have characterized the episode as a textbook public meltdown, suggesting that even figures of his stature are not immune to the gravitational pull of online humiliation.
clips.text_en_c2: Elon Musk took to his platform to lament that chess, with its combinatorial vastness, exceeds the cognitive capacity of unaided human players and ought therefore to be outsourced to artificial agents. Chess.com's official account responded with a trio of consecutive ratio replies, each more pointed than the last, reducing his grievance to absurdity in real time. Rather than concede the exchange, Musk pivoted to promising that robotic chess will, in due course, render organic play obsolete, before dismissing the operator behind the account as a mere intern — a transparently desperate feint that the community duly catalogued as a textbook public meltdown. The spectacle, were one charitably inclined, might be read as exhaustion; the uncharitable interpretation, and the prevailing one online, was simply pathetic.

clips.text_zh: /v/ 又有人問點解西方選手唔跟 developer 嘅規則。S15 啦兄弟，人哋玩 Meta 同我哋唔同，仲要解釋到幾時。睇完算。
clips.text_en_b1: A /v/ poster asks why Western players cannot follow entirely reasonable rules from game developers. The thread compares how Eastern and Western pro scenes interpret patch notes and competitive rulings, with most replies blaming ego and bad coaching more than the rules themselves.
clips.source_hint: /v/ thread asking why Western players keep ignoring developer rules

signal.rationale: Esports culture thread, no trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: A /v/ poster is once again asking why Western competitive players consistently ignore entirely reasonable rulings issued by game developers. Although the thread compares how Eastern and Western pro scenes interpret patch notes and competitive rules, most respondents tend to blame inflated egos and poor coaching rather than the rules themselves. With Season 15 already in full swing, the frustration clearly isn't going anywhere.
clips.text_en_c1: A poster on /v/ has once again posed the perennial question of why Western competitive players appear incapable of adhering to what most consider entirely reasonable directives from the development team. The ensuing thread draws comparisons between the Eastern circuit, where patch notes and official rulings are internalized with near-religious deference, and the Western scene, which tends to treat any restrictive guideline as a starting point for creative interpretation. The prevailing consensus attributes the divergence less to the rules themselves than to entrenched egos and coaching infrastructures that reward individual flair over disciplined execution, a tension that, were it ever resolved, would reshape the meta overnight.
clips.text_en_c2: A poster on /v/ has reignited the perennial inquiry as to why Western competitors so persistently disregard the ostensibly reasonable directives issued by game developers. The thread quickly metastasised into a comparative autopsy of regional competitive cultures: Eastern rosters, long acculturated to a deference bordering on the ritualistic, tend to internalise patch notes and rulings as gospel, whereas Western imports treat such pronouncements as merely advisory, subordinate to the perceived meta and to individual ego. Several respondents laid the blame less at the feet of the developers than at those of head coaches who permit, even encourage, such insubordination as a performative signal of competitive identity. The discussion resolved, as these discussions invariably do, into a weary shrug and a changed tab.

clips.text_zh: 個 bench 315lbs 都被人摺埋。肥仔信睇完應該笑我。Grappling 真係要 join，但又驚時間唔夠，考牌都未搞掂。
clips.text_en_b1: Someone with an impressive 315 lbs bench press can still be folded in half by a much lighter grappler. The thread argues there is no excuse not to train grappling, unless you want a guy 50 pounds lighter to turn you into his bitch. Even a half-decent grappler will have you staring at your own asshole in seconds.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread arguing every lifter needs grappling because size does not save you

signal.rationale: Fitness culture rant, no trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: Someone capable of benching an impressive 315 pounds can still get folded in half by a much lighter grappler with solid fundamentals. The thread makes the case that there is genuinely no excuse for skipping grappling training, unless you genuinely enjoy letting a guy fifty pounds lighter turn you into his bitch. Even a half-decent grappler will have you staring at the ceiling in seconds.
clips.text_en_c1: A lifter capable of pressing 315 pounds on the bench can, with almost comical ease, be folded into a pretzel by a grappler weighing a mere fraction of that figure. The thread makes the case, with characteristic bluntness, that no rational excuse exists for neglecting grappling training, unless one derives genuine pleasure from being systematically dismantled by someone fifty pounds lighter. Even a modestly competent practitioner of Brazilian jiu-jitsu will, within seconds, position an opponent in such a way that the latter finds himself contemplating his own navel from an orientation nature never sanctioned, a humbling experience that the bench press alone cannot remediate.
clips.text_en_c2: A bencher capable of pressing 315 pounds — genuinely impressive by any gymnasium standard — can still be folded like laundry by a grappling opponent half his weight, provided that opponent has invested even a few months in competent instruction. The thread's consensus was unforgiving: there exists no defensible excuse for neglecting grappling training, unless one relishes the prospect of being routinely submitted, inverted, and forced into an intimate acquaintance with one's own navel by technicians of markedly inferior mass. Striking confers the illusion of control; grappling confers the reality of it. Practitioners who dismiss the discipline on grounds of insufficient time discover, almost without exception, that the time was always available — it was merely allocated elsewhere, and to poorer ends.

clips.text_zh: Yani Neko 當 AOTY，毒品、體液、貧窮都畫出嚟，唔係表面咁簡單。廢柴如我都覺得有意義，考牌後要開黎睇。
clips.text_en_b1: Yani Neko is being called the greatest work of counterculture art to come out of anime in years. Critics say viewers get upset over its gross-out humor, sexual comedy, and substance abuse references, but those elements are real, not just shock value. The comedy framing hides a genuinely raw portrait of poverty and bodies.
clips.source_hint: /a/ thread making the case for Yani Neko as anime of the year counterculture pick

signal.rationale: Anime discourse thread, no trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: Yani Neko is increasingly being called the most significant work of counterculture art to emerge from anime in years, largely because its gross-out humor, explicit sexual comedy, and unflinching references to substance abuse refuse to play it safe. Although casual viewers often dismiss these elements as mere shock value, the comedy framing actually conceals a genuinely raw portrait of poverty and bodily existence.
clips.text_en_c1: Yani Neko has emerged as a strong contender for anime of the year, largely on the strength of its reputation as a countercultural work whose surface grotesquerie has alienated audiences unprepared for its ambition. Critics contend that the series deploys bodily fluids, recreational substance abuse, and abrasive sexual comedy not as gratuitous provocation but as a deliberate aesthetic vocabulary through which poverty, precarity, and the unglamorous textures of working-class existence are rendered with disarming honesty. The comedic scaffolding, in this reading, functions as a Trojan horse for a portrait whose rawness would otherwise be commercially untenable, an argument that converts the show from mere shock into something approaching genuine art.
clips.text_en_c2: Yani Neko has, with mounting critical consensus, been nominated as the foremost work of artistic dissent to emerge from the anime medium in recent memory. Detractors recoil at its scatological set pieces, its unflinching sexual humour, and its frankly rendered depictions of substance abuse, mistaking these for gratuitous provocation when they function, in fact, as the work's essential vernacular. Beneath the veneer of juvenile comedy lies a lacerating examination of economic precarity, bodily degradation, and the quiet indignities inflicted upon those whom polite society has elected to overlook. The laughter, the creators seem to insist, is a coping mechanism; the discomfort, the point. For viewers willing to sit with the squirm, the rewards are considerable — and, mercifully, no prerequisite certification is required to begin.
